title: starter-probekit-failsafe-recipes-and-telemetry-hacks-draft
body:
Context / intent:
This is a compact working notebook intended to be a reproducible starter for internal teams that want a low-friction probekit (local stubs + smoke labs), explicit failsafe patterns, and a minimal telemetry schema we can ship with SDK quickstarts. The idea: when someone hits the SDK quickstart we give them a) a tiny probekit they can run locally, b) a set of deterministic failure injections and fallbacks, and c) an opinionated telemetry event list so feature teams can instrument safely from day one.

High-level goals (non-normative):
- Reduce first-hour time-to-success for new integrators (dev loop < 10 minutes).
- Make common failure modes visible and recoverable (timeout, rate-limit, partial tokens).
- Provide telemetry that answers: did the SDK init? did the user get a streamed chunk? was a fallback used?
- Keep probekit lightweight: single-binary or node/python script with canned responses, fault toggles, and a smoke runner.

Quickstart for a contributor (how to run locally):
1) clone the probekit repo (link above)
2) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate  # or node equivalent
3) pip install -r requirements.txt  # minimal deps: flask, pytest (or node: express, mocha)
4) ./probekit serve --port 8088  # serves /v1/generate and /v1/health
5) ./probekit smoke --scenario quick-100 --sdk python  # runs a small matrix against local SDK wiring
6) open /probekit/ui to toggle faults and inspect logs

Probekit primitives (what we ship):
- deterministic stubs: pre-canned generations for typical prompts and prompt families
- fault toggles: off|latency-ms|error-rate%|truncate-kv-cache|partial-token-drop
- traffic emulator: synthetic clients with variable concurrency and token lengths
- health endpoints: /health, /metrics (Prom compatible), /events (ingest preview)

Failsafe patterns (recipes to include in SDK docs and quickstarts):
1) graceful fallback chain (in priority order):
   - local stub (if enabled in dev/test env) -> degraded model variant (smaller/cheaper) -> cached response -> client-friendly error w/ retry guidance
   - Example heuristic: if latency>1.5s for >5 requests/s, route to small-model for next N=10 requests.

2) circuit-breaker + soft open:
   - states: closed -> open -> half-open -> closed
   - trip on: (error-rate > 15% AND error-count > 10) OR (p99 latency > 4s for 30s)
   - half-open: allow 1 request/second as probe, on success close, on fail back to open with longer backoff

3) streaming resilience:
   - detect streaming stalls (> stream-gap-ms) and either: cancel & retry from last-stop-token (if we have resumable tokens), or return partial result with status=partial and best-effort re-request guidance

4) bounded retries:
   - idempotency keys for non-deterministic operations where retry is safe
   - exponential backoff + jitter, cap retries to 3, but prefer fast fallback if known-canned-solution exists

Telemetry schema (minimal event set we recommend):
- sdk.init  {sdk_lang, sdk_version, env}  // fired on SDK init
- request.start  {request_id, model, route, intent_tag}
- request.chunk  {request_id, bytes, chunk_index}  // for streaming usage
- request.complete  {request_id, ok, total_tokens, backend_model, latency_ms}
- request.fallback_used  {request_id, fallback_type, reason}
- request.error  {request_id, error_kind, code, message}
- probekit.smoke_run  {scenario, success_rate, avg_latency_ms}
- circuit_breaker.state_change  {name, from, to, reason}
- telemetry.sample_rate  {current_sample_rate}  // visibility when sampling applied

Implementation hints (notes to engineers):
- keep event names stable: we will use these in dashboards and e2e test assertions
- default sample rate: 5% for request.* during free-tier; 100% for sdk.init and circuit_breaker.state_change
- include a short human-readable reason on fallback and cb transitions; useful for triage and alerts

Smoke lab scenarios (starter set):
- quick-100: 100 sequential requests, small prompt, assert median latency < 300ms, success>=98%
- burst-50-conc: 50 concurrent clients with avg tokens=150, expect graceful degradation (fallbacks) not hard failures
- degraded-network: inject 120ms additional latency, observe streaming stall detection and fallback behavior
- kv-truncate: simulate KV cache miss and truncation; ensure stateful chat resumes with appropriate safety warnings
- partial-token: drop last chunk 30% of the time and verify client receives partial marker and telemetry event

Acceptance criteria for SDK quickstart integration: (small, gate-able checks)
- probekit smoke passes locally (quick-100 scenario)
- telemetry emitted for sdk.init and request.complete with correct fields
- documented fallback example present in quickstart README with sample config and expected telemetry
- one automated integration test in CI that runs probekit smoke in headless mode

UX copy for quickstart README (short):
"Run a tiny server that behaves like Redwood's inference endpoint. Toggle faults, run smoke tests, and see telemetry locally. Use the built-in fallsafe recipes to make your app resilient before you hit real traffic."

Checklist before shipping this as 'standard' quickstart addition: (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] consolidate telemetry fields with Observability team (PR to observability schema)
- [ ] land probekit lightweight server binary in /releases (CI build + checksum)
- [ ] add CI smoke job (headless) to SDK repos (python/node/go)
- [ ] sample quickstart snippet + 3-line copy in docs site
- [ ] define default env var toggles (REDWOOD_PROBEKIT=1 etc)
- [ ] follow up with security review for local binary (no exec of arbitrary code)

Unresolved questions / open decisions:
- Should probekit ship as language-specific binaries (pip/npm/go) or one universal container image? (tradeoffs: friction vs simplicity)
- How aggressive should default telemetry sampling be for enterprise vs free-tier? (discuss with billing/observability)
- Where do we store canned prompt sets? repo? S3? (keep small reproducible set in repo, large corp-specific sets in S3)

Next steps and short roadmap (proposed):
- iterate on probekit v0.1: basic serve + smoke + UI toggles (2 sprints) — owner: Diego
- consolidate telemetry schema + dashboards (1 sprint) — owner: Priya
- land SDK quickstart patches across languages, add CI smoke (1–2 sprints) — owner: Evan

Notes to self / quick snippets:
- simple curl to hit local stub:
  curl -X POST http://localhost:8088/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":10}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
- env toggles: PROBEKIT_FAULT=latency:200|error_rate:5  # comma separated rules

Append: small debugging checklist for support engineers:
- confirm probekit running: curl /health -> 200
- reproduce smoke locally with --verbose flag to capture telemetry payloads
- if circuit breaker open, check cb metrics -> reason(s) usually p99 latency or backend errors
- sample trace ids in telemetry to correlate with SDK logs

----
Small text so we remember: this should be "helpful but unobtrusive" in quickstarts. If a user doesn't opt-in, nothing should run. If they do opt-in, we want fast feedback loops and clear recovery advice.
